From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved commit term options, staging protections, and ramp cadence — SprintAI

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I want to put three concrete reserved-commit options on the table so your procurement and engineering teams can evaluate trade-offs quickly: 12m / 24m / 36m. The attached "Committed_Offer_SprintAI_v1.pdf" summarizes pricing, committed GPU vCPU-equivalents, and the baseline throughput SLOs per tier. I also attached a scenario workbook (capacity_model_scenarioB.xlsx) showing expected token throughput and cost per 1M tokens under different batch/quantization mixes.

A few implementation notes and questions we need to align on:
- Start window: we can provision Dedicated capacity to be available as early as Sep 15, 2026, but a staged rollout (50% capacity first 30 days, 100% at day 90) helps reduce wasted baseline when usage is still ramping.
- Staging protection: we can add a 3–6 month "staging buffer" where unused committed capacity accrues as credits to be applied later in the term (or against overage in the following month). This is optional and affects discounting.
- Throughput guarantee: we provide per-route p95 latency and per-GPU throughput commitments in the SLA. For shortfalls we offer service credits; for prolonged shortfalls (>14 days) we will propose a capacity remap or temporary uplift at Redwood expense.

Please review the attached offer and the workbook with your engineering/procurement folks. Specific asks for your team:
1) Which term do you prefer to evaluate first (12/24/36)?
2) Do you want the 3-month staging buffer (yes/no)?
3) Any constraints from procurement on early termination or attrition protections they require?

If it helps, Karthik and I can put together a 30-minute redline session with procurement this week to walk through the commercial trade-offs and the contract language we typically include for attrition protection.

Thanks —

--
Priyom Das

Priyom —

Appreciate the clear breakdown and the workbook — helpful. Quick answers from our side:
- Preference: we are inclined toward a 24-month term if the commercial is favorable; 12m has too much volatility for our forecasts and 36m is a large operational commitment for us right now.
- Staging buffer: we like the idea of a 3-month buffer, but procurement will want firm language on how credits accrue and expire.
- Attrition / early termination: procurement asked whether there is a mechanism for headcount/usage reduction (e.g., if we spin down a product) — they'd prefer a decommit step or a true-down with a capped credit schedule rather than a pure early-termination fee.

Also attached a short SOW outline (SOW_draft_SprintAI.docx) that lists our expected start features and a proposed pilot schedule. Two asks before we can move a redline:
1) Can you give an example short-form clause for "staging buffer credits" and the expiration logic?
2) What discount could you offer if we commit to a 24m term with a 6-month ramp to full capacity? Procurement will want real $/GPU-month numbers to model against other vendors.

Would like to review with your sales/legal on Thursday morning PT if possible.

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Reserved commit term options, staging protections, and ramp cadence — SprintAI

Hi Samira / Priyom —

Thanks for the notes. Looping in a practical counterproposal that balances SprintAI's need for flexibility with the economic certainty we need to support Dedicated pools. Key points below (summary first, legal/commercial language we can provide as examples in the redline session):

Proposed commercial structure (24-month primary path):
- Term: 24 months (preferred).
- Pricing: 18% discount vs list for the first 12 months at target commit; 22% discount for months 13–24 if usage stays within 85–120% of baseline commit.
- Ramp: 6-month staged ramp to full committed capacity: Month 0–1 = 25%, Month 2–3 = 60%, Month 4–6 = 100%. Credits for unused committed capacity will accrue monthly and can be applied as on-invoice credits for months 7–12 only. Any accrued credits remaining at month 12 convert to a one-time overage credit capped at 15% of yearly committed spend.
- Attrition / true-down: One true-down allowed in months 9–12 with a 10% true-down cap for the remainder of the term; early termination outside of the true-down window triggers a declining early-termination schedule (months 1–6 = 60% of remaining committed value, months 7–12 = 40%, thereafter 25%).
- Throughput guarantees & remediation: We commit to p95 latency and per-GPU throughput. Operational credits for shortfall: first 3 days = operational support / mitigation; 4–14 days = pro-rata service credit; >14 days = credit + capacity reshuffle at our cost for week 1 of remediation.

Why this helps SprintAI: predictable unit economics with a reasonable buffer for product ramp, ability to true-down once as product priorities shift, and a capped exposure for both sides if usage materially deviates. It also lets us discount more aggressively in months 13–24 as we amortize the Dedicated pool.

I can draft specific contract clauses this afternoon and we'll walk them through on Thursday. Priyom — please add the sample pricing table to the offer PDF and include an example invoice math for the first 12 months (showing staging credits applied).

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales
